aircraft.engine: Pratt & Whitney PW4000, GE CF6-80, or Rolls-Royce RB211-524 series
aircraft.source: Maximum operating altitude (43,100 ft) confirmed directly from an FAA Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS AV-0301) — a primary regulatory document, the strongest sourcing in this file set. Mmo (0.86) corroborated across two independent sources. No published climb/descent table was found for this type; the table here is extrapolated from typical widebody twin performance.
aircraft.source_confidence: LIMITS ARE HIGH CONFIDENCE (primary FAA document for ceiling). CLIMB/DESCENT TABLE IS AN EXTRAPOLATION, not sourced from a 767-specific published profile — treat with the same skepticism as the B752 table.

climb.reference_condition: Typical airline climb profile, moderate weight, ISA. Speed schedule: 250 KIAS below FL100, ~310-320 KIAS climb.
climb.notes: EXTRAPOLATED — no 767-specific published climb table found. Widebody twins of this class typically show somewhat lower ROC than narrowbodies at a given density altitude due to higher typical operating weights; this table reflects that general pattern rather than a 767-specific certified figure.

cruise.notes: Max range speed reported at Mach 0.81; economic/typical cruise commonly cited near Mach 0.80. Mmo of 0.86 gives a comfortable margin above typical cruise.

descent.reference_condition: Typical idle-thrust descent, Mach 0.80 / ~310 KIAS / 250 KIAS below FL100
descent.notes: No 767-specific published descent table found. Follows the standard ~3nm-per-1000ft industry planning rule.
